candidates.summary: -home is relative to the output dir but gnodev's -C chdirs before it is resolved, so the node home lands in <root>/examples/_preview/.gnodev-<port> and the workflow's rm -rf _preview/.gnodev-* deletes nothing
candidates.failure_scenario: render runs from the repo root with -out _preview. startGnodev passes -home _preview/.gnodev-8899 together with -C <root>/examples, and gnodev's execLocalApp calls os.Chdir(cfg.chdir) as its first statement (contribs/gnodev/command_local.go:87-89), before any use of -home. The datadir, genesis and keybase are therefore created at <root>/examples/_preview/.gnodev-8899, inside the checked-out source tree; the base pass leaves a second one at <base-root>/examples/_preview/.gnodev-8900. pr-preview.yml's cleanup, rm -rf _preview/gnodev.log _preview/gnodev-base.log _preview/.gnodev-*, and its du -sh _preview both look at <root>/_preview and see neither, so the line that is supposed to keep the node home out of the published snapshot is a no-op and the homes accumulate on any reused runner or local checkout.

candidates.summary: a PR that changes only a p/ package renders its dependent realms and gets no picture at all: the pairs branch needs ChangedRealms and the sample branch needs Gnoweb
candidates.failure_scenario: changed.txt holds examples/gno.land/p/demo/x/x.gno alone. BuildPlan files that package under ChangedPkgs, leaves ChangedRealms empty, sets Gnoweb false, and fills Realms with every realm importing it. render's `if len(plan.ChangedRealms) > 0 { pairs } else if plan.Gnoweb { shots }` takes neither branch, so preview.json carries no pairs and no shots and the comment is a list of links. candidates.summary: the base crawl's page cap is exactly its seed count, and the cap is a hard error renderBase swallows to stderr, so one extra queued page deletes every before/after silently
candidates.failure_scenario: base := &Crawler{MaxPages: len(realms), RenderOnly: true} has zero headroom: Seeds() yields exactly one URL per realm while RenderOnly is set, and Run checks len(c.pages) >= MaxPages before each fetch, so the cap is unreachable only as long as that stays true. Give the base pass one more page -- a $source view of the changed file, a seed reached twice under a different spelling, a retry that records a page -- and Run returns "page cap N reached"; renderBase prints "  ! base render:" to stderr and returns nil, ScreenshotPairs then emits after-only pairs, and the comment shows no comparison while the job stays green. The head crawl gets 400 pages for the same work.
